Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay} plots the binary pairwise AUC decay curves.
For Pythia-1.4B (nucleus), AUC decays monotonically: d0-vs-d1 $= 0.999$, d1-vs-d2 $= 0.925$, d2-vs-d3 $= 0.823$, d3-vs-d4 $= 0.784$, d4-vs-d5 $= 0.683$.
The steepest drop occurs between the d1-vs-d2 and d2-vs-d3 pairs; the curve then flattens as the system approaches an indistinguishable regime gradually rather than crossing a sharp boundary.

\paragraph{Cross-model convergence at depth 4--5.}
All three models exhibit a consistent profile at the deep boundaries.
The d3-vs-d4 AUC clusters near the $T{=}0.75$ threshold: Pythia $0.784$ (bootstrap 95\% CI $[0.765, 0.802]$, $p = 0.001$), OLMo $0.765$ ($[0.744, 0.785]$, $p = 0.091$), GPT-2~XL $0.750$ ($[0.728, 0.771]$, $p = 0.505$), where $p$ denotes the one-tailed bootstrap probability under $H_0\!: \mathrm{AUC} \leq 0.75$ (1{,}000 iterations).
Only Pythia achieves significance at conventional levels; OLMo is marginal and GPT-2~XL falls on the threshold despite its higher in-distribution accuracy.
The d4-vs-d5 AUC falls uniformly below 0.70 across all three models (Pythia $0.683$, OLMo $0.684$, GPT-2~XL $0.681$), confirming a model-independent signal saturation point at depth~5.

This pattern---directional consistency across models with graded statistical strength---supports interpreting the d3--d4 region as a \emph{transition zone} rather than a binary boundary.
The continuous AUC decay curve provides a more informative characterization of depth discriminability than any single $\mathrm{EDD}_T$ value.

lines: \paragraph{Decision boundary dilution.}
\label{sec:atlas:edd:dilution}

EDD's binary-pair design is motivated by \emph{decision boundary dilution}: when a multi-class classifier must simultaneously separate $K$ depths, its decision boundaries are shared across all $\binom{K}{2}$ class pairs, diluting the capacity allocated to any single adjacent pair.

-Concretely, in the Pythia nucleus setting (experiment \texttt{granularity\_ablation\_rf\_001}), the d2\,vs.\,d3 pairwise AUC degrades from 0.804 in a 4-class pipeline to 0.689 in a 6-class pipeline---a 14.3\% relative decline---despite identical underlying data.

+Concretely, in the Pythia nucleus setting, the d2\,vs.\,d3 pairwise AUC degrades from 0.804 in a 4-class pipeline to 0.689 in a 6-class pipeline---a 14.3\% relative decline---despite identical underlying data.
Mean classification accuracy likewise drops from 99.5\% (binary) to 78.3\% (4-class) to 62.9\% (6-class).
Because the pairwise signal between depths $d$ and $d{+}1$ does not change when unrelated depths are added, this degradation is entirely attributable to boundary dilution, not signal loss.
Binary pairwise classifiers eliminate this confound, isolating the true adjacent-pair discriminability that EDD is designed to measure.

lines: Starting from a Wikipedia subset as seed text ($\mathcal{D}_0$), each generation cycle proceeds in three steps: (1)~LoRA finetuning \cite{hu2022lora} with rank $r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$, learning rate $2{\times}10^{-4}$, batch size 8, for 3 epochs; (2)~generation of 5{,}000 passages (max 512 tokens) under the specified decoding strategy; (3)~the generated corpus becomes $\mathcal{D}_k$ and serves as training data for the next cycle.
Each generation cycle samples unconditionally from the BOS token; there is no per-passage lineage across depths, ensuring that cross-validation splits do not introduce information leakage.

LoRA targets are architecture-specific: \texttt{query\_key\_value} for Pythia (GPT-NeoX), \texttt{q\_proj}/\texttt{k\_proj}/\texttt{v\_proj} for OLMo, and \texttt{c\_attn}/\texttt{c\_proj} for GPT-2~XL.

Given a threshold $T$, we define:
\begin{equation}
-\mathrm{EDD}_T = \max \{ d^*{+}1 : \mathrm{AUC}(d^*, d^*{+}1) \geq T \}
+\mathrm{EDD}_T = \max \bigl\{ d^*{+}1 : \forall\, d' \leq d^*,\; \mathrm{AUC}(d', d'{+}1) \geq T \bigr\}
\label{eq:edd}
\end{equation}

+where $d^* \in \{0, 1, \dots, K{-}1\}$.\footnote{In our data, pairwise AUC decreases monotonically with depth across all configurations tested, so the universal quantifier ($\forall d' \leq d^*$) and the simpler $\max\{d^*{+}1 : \mathrm{AUC}(d^*, d^*{+}1) \geq T\}$ yield identical values.  The $\forall$ formulation is preferred because it guarantees a contiguous discriminable range, which the pointwise version does not when AUC is non-monotonic.}
The default threshold is $T{=}0.75$; we report sensitivity analyses at $T \in \{0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80\}$ in \S\ref{sec:atlas}.

Crucially, each AUC is obtained from an independent binary pairwise classifier (5-fold stratified CV) rather than extracted from a single multi-class model, avoiding decision boundary dilution (\S\ref{sec:atlas}).

\paragraph{EDD monotonicity assumption.}
Our EDD definition (Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}) requires all pairwise AUCs up to depth $d^*$ to exceed $T$, which is well-behaved when AUC decays monotonically---as observed in all our configurations.
However, \citet{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement} show that early recursion can temporarily \emph{improve} model quality, which could produce non-monotonic AUC profiles (e.g., a dip at d1/d2 followed by recovery at d2/d3).
In such cases EDD would conservatively report a lower value than the deepest discriminable pair, potentially underestimating the true discriminable range; extending EDD to handle non-contiguous discriminable regions is future work.
